package http

import (
	"encoding/json"
	"net/http"

	"metaldocs/internal/platform/problem"
)

// A3.1 negative fixture: a delivery package growing its own thirteenth
// writeProblem. This is the exact shape that produced G-07 — twelve packages
// each owning status, Content-Type, marshalling and (inconsistently) logging,
// so "the API's error contract" was whatever twelve files happened to agree on.
//
// Two independent properties are proven here, and both must be reported:
//
//   - the SIGNATURE rule: a function taking an http.ResponseWriter together
//     with a *problem.Problem is a serializer, whatever it is named. Renaming
//     it emitErr or respondProblem must not buy an exemption.
//   - the MEDIA TYPE rule: writing "application/problem+json" by hand is the
//     other half of the clone. problem.Write is unexported, so this is the only
//     remaining way to rebuild the envelope.
//
// If a future edit collapsed the two rules into one, one of the Want strings in
// the arch-lint fixture stops appearing and this fixture fails — which is how
// "both halves are enforced" stays a fact rather than a comment.
//
// See scripts/testdata/guard-fixtures/README.md.
func writeProblem(w http.ResponseWriter, p *problem.Problem) {
	payload, err := json.Marshal(p)
	if err != nil {
		w.WriteHeader(http.StatusInternalServerError)
		return
	}
	w.Header().Set("Content-Type", "application/problem+json")
	w.WriteHeader(p.Status)
	_, _ = w.Write(payload)
}
